candidates.review_note: The task is textual. A power beginning with N satisfies log10(N)+k <= e log10(2) < log10(N+1)+k, with k>=digits(N)+1; equivalently e>=ceil(2*digits/log10(2)) and the fractional part lies in a fixed interval. Count interval hits up to a candidate exponent using the difference of two floor sums; evaluate each floor sum by Euclidean lattice-count reciprocity rather than iterating billions of suffix lengths for 32-bit prefixes. Binary-search the first hit after exponential bracketing. Compute with Decimal at 80 and 120 significant digits and require agreement; this is a high-precision numeric algorithm, not a claim of symbolic logarithm proof. Positive prefixes have hits because log10(2) is irrational; zero cannot lead a positive power. Public tests compare exact small integer powers and an independent suffix-length search, plus direct high-precision inequalities for large prefixes. Count only eligible exponents starting at the digit-length threshold: including small exact powers at excluded prefix endpoints can introduce numerical cancellation at an exact integer floor boundary. The original candidate precision-disagreement failure is retained.
